target.title: fix(cron): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in job patch helpers
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `applyJobPatch`, `mergeCronDelivery`, and `mergeCronFailureAlert` to prevent prototype chain pollution when applying cron job patches.

## What Problem This Solves
The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties. When a cron job patch comes from a JSON-parsed HTTP request body, a prototype-polluted key (e.g., `"description"` injected into `Object.prototype` by a malicious dependency) would be incorrectly detected as present in an empty patch `{}`, causing the job to be silently mutated with attacker-controlled values.

**Code evidence**: In `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, 23 locations use `"key" in patch` across three functions (`applyJobPatch`, `mergeCronDelivery`, `mergeCronFailureAlert`). The file already uses `Object.hasOwn` correctly for `existingFd` checks (lines 1154–1164), but inconsistently uses `in` for `patchFd` in the same code block (lines 1167–1182) and elsewhere.

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain; `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) checks only own properties
- This is the third fix in the series: #99152 (config redact-snapshot) and #99129 (markdown-core frontmatter) used the same pattern
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase — these 23 were the remaining `in` operator usages on untrusted patch objects in the cron subsystem

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 23-line change, 1 file, no behavioral impact on normal keys
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage both within this file and across the codebase (#99129, #99152)
- **Defense-in-depth**: even though current checked keys (`name`, `description`, `channel`, etc.) are not on `Object.prototype`, prototype pollution from malicious dependencies could add them

## User Impact
- **Affected**: cron job PATCH operations via REST API or CLI
- **Before**: a prototype-polluted object could inject values into job fields unexpectedly
- **After**: only own properties of the patch object are applied; inherited prototype properties are ignored

## Evidence

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-cron-hasown.mjs
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "description" into job (got: INJECTED_DESC)
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "name" into job (got: INJECTED_NAME)
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "failureAlert" into job (got: {})
PASS: "toString" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "constructor" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "valueOf" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "hasOwnProperty" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: normal keys work — name="renamed-ok", description="valid description"

3 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-cron-hasown.mjs
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "description" — job protected
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "name" — job protected
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "failureAlert" — job protected
PASS: "toString" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "constructor" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "valueOf" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "hasOwnProperty" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: normal keys work — name="renamed-ok", description="valid description"

ALL 8 PASS
```

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-cron-hasown.mjs
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "description" into job (got: INJECTED_DESC)
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "name" into job (got: INJECTED_NAME)
FAIL: empty patch leaked prototype "failureAlert" into job (got: {})
PASS: "toString" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "constructor" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "valueOf" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "hasOwnProperty" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: normal keys work — name="renamed-ok", description="valid description"

3 FAILED
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-cron-hasown.mjs
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "description" — job protected
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "name" — job protected
PASS: empty patch did NOT leak prototype "failureAlert" — job protected
PASS: "toString" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "constructor" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "valueOf" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: "hasOwnProperty" — in=true hasOwn=false (prototype chain vs own property)
PASS: normal keys work — name="renamed-ok", description="valid description"

ALL 8 PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- Regression test added to `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` covering the 4 standard `Object.prototype` keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) using `it.each`
- All 81 existing + new tests pass
- `pnpm check`: TypeScript compilation passes (pre-existing `npm shrinkwrap guard` failure is unrelated)
- Diff: 2 files, +45 / −23 lines
